item.title: I am reviewer?
item.content:encoded:
It is quite fun to see my username. How does this work per module?

Also, I do live near Temecula. I'm glad that you took my advice to to make Ambrose on the casual dining budget level. Quite reflective of the region's somewhat conservative atmosphere.

item.content:encoded: The fact that I saw my own review was hilarious.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I guess my biggest concern is the actual menu items: why?

I know this is supposed to be the… do we have a name for this shared universe? SCP seems too Foundation-centric. Either way, I know this is supposed to be anomalous food, and that's fine! But for some of these, my biggest question is why. Why would an entity whose existence allows for the safe consumption of food want to remove friction? What, besides novelty1, would drive someone to turn either Ambrose or brought food (itself iffy for a restaurant) into potato wedges, and while I'm at it, how is that a main dish? If the Gangster's Grub is a fight between two foods, what are those two foods, and if it really is random each time, what measures should Ambrose take to make sure Johnson "Peanuts Will Literally Kill Me Dead" McDickcheese isn't gonna waste money on a pad thai that just put an Elvis sandwich in a chokehold?

This feels less like a menu of things people would actually want to eat, and more wacky culinary endeavors spearheaded by the kind of people who don't eat what they cook.

Footnotes
1. And if I'm answering my own question, I'm forced to admit that I've grown somewhat tired of "the anomalous as purely novelty" myself.

I had the same "mom and pop" restaurant objection. That was mitigated somewhat by this being a smaller, deliberately less upscale franchise than the flagship restaurant in 3Ports. Nonetheless, the menu items were good writing and the reviews told a fun story. This still gets my upvote.

item.title: Re: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
The image from SCP-1325 is a doctored version if this image. It's CC 2.0, so you'll be okay to the best of my knowledge.

EDIT: My opinions on the piece.

The presentation is good. I really like the menu's looks and the care that went into designing it, it's very obvious this is a passion project. The listpage module was cute, too. My only nit to pick as far as presentation goes are that it looks like the menu of a mom and pop restaurant, which Ambrose pretty obviously is not.

Unfortunately, I'm left a little underwhelmed by the contents of the article.

The menu is full of fun little anomalies, which are fun to read and don't overstay their welcome. The problem comes from the reviews at the bottom. This might be due to my ignorance, but how does the average person here know about the Foundation?1 A customer threatens the restaurant by calling the full might of the Foundation on them. Somehow. There's no story being told in the reviews either, just a bunch of loosely related events happening that don't tie into anything.

If I had to summarize my issues with this, it would come down to 'style over substance.' It looks good, but ultimately is too small a serving and the taste leaves a lot to be desired.

Footnotes
1. In a discussion with a fellow user, they mentioned the Broken Masquerade canon being a possibility here. If this is the case, I cannot tell if it was intended.
